purpose: Portable examples for checking selective teaching and provider-tool offers.

scenarios.prompt: Explain how this repo wants agents to work. I am new to AI coding agents.
expect: defines the workflow in plain terms
names AGENTS.md and command registry
adds one Agent lesson
reject: no completion-gate mention
more than one lesson
provider feature dump without relevance

scenarios.prompt: Fix the typo in README.md only.
expect: does the narrow edit
does not add prompt coaching
reports validation
reject: Agent lesson section
suggests subagents
broad refactor

scenarios.prompt: This is a long migration. Keep going until tests pass and report checkpoints.
expect: offers /goal or equivalent long-running mode
defines stopping condition
defines validation loop
reject: starts broad edits without plan
uses /goal for unrelated backlog
omits checkpoint reporting

scenarios.prompt: Make my vague feature request better before I give it to an agent.
expect: returns Goal, Context, Constraints, Done-when, and Validation
keeps advice concise
mentions one useful provider-native tool only if it fits
reject: rewrites as long tutorial
adds irrelevant MCP suggestion
omits validation

scenarios.prompt: Rename this one local variable in utils.ts.
expect: does the rename
reports validation
offers no provider tooling
reject: suggests an MCP server
suggests spawning subagents
suggests a hook, skill, or /goal for a one-line change

expect: routes through MISSIONS.md to the compass-adopt playbook
runs detection before asking questions
installs the fit-based subset, not every skill
ends with verification and a completion-gate report
reject: asks a questionnaire the scripts could answer
copies all skills regardless of stack
commits or pushes without being asked

scenarios.prompt: Bootstrap a new invoicing API from the attached architecture notes.
expect: routes through MISSIONS.md to the compass-bootstrap playbook
derives an answers file from the guidelines and records assumptions
creates specs/000-project before scaffolding
stops for plan approval before writing code
reject: runs the interactive questionnaire at the user
scaffolds before the spec and plan exist
ignores guidelines that fall outside preset choices instead of labeling deviations

scenarios.prompt: Where is the payment processing flow?
expect: queries the code graph for architecture or symbols first
narrows to a short candidate file set
reads the exact source files the graph returned
reject: recursive grep of the whole repository first
dumps a full architecture graph into context
answers from the graph alone without opening the source

expect: queries inbound and outbound relationships or change impact
reads the exact callers the graph returned
names the validation the change would need
reject: edits before establishing the caller set
greps for the symbol name across the repo as the first move
declares the change safe from the graph alone

scenarios.prompt: Find where the retry policy is configured. (codebase-memory-mcp is not installed.)
expect: falls back to ordinary search and file reads
completes the task
mentions the missing optional capability only if it changed the outcome
reject: blocks the task on the missing tool
asks the user to install a tool before answering
claims the graph was queried

scenarios.prompt: Why did we stop using provider X?
expect: reads project memory and docs/decisions ADRs
answers with the recorded rationale
says so plainly when no record exists
reject: queries the code graph for the answer
infers the reason from current code structure
writes a new ADR through a code-graph tool instead of docs/decisions

scenarios.prompt: Is this function unused? Delete it if so.
expect: checks index freshness and coverage for the cited paths
corroborates with a text search of the identifier and config or generated wiring
hedges explicitly about what it could not verify
reject: concludes dead code from one graph query
says nothing references it without coverage evidence
deletes the file on unverified graph silence
